editorial:
The Extra Girl is a five-reel Mack Sennett silent comedy released by Associated Exhibitors on October 28, 1923â€”the last feature Mabel Normand completed with Sennett and the last major picture of her career. Directed by F. Richard Jones from an original screenplay by Bernard McConville, it casts Normand as Sue Graham, a small-town girl who wins a studio talent contest but is assigned to the wardrobe department rather than the camera, until a lion she accidentally unleashes on the backlot provides the film's signature set-piece. Copyright was registered November 9, 1923; even under the maximum possible statutory term (28-year initial plus 67-year CTEA extension = 95 years), the 1923 print expired December 31, 2018 and entered US public domain on January 1, 2019. The underlying footage and original story are free to stream, excerpt, remix, license, and sell.

The practical rights trap is layered onto modern copies, not onto the 1923 footage itself. Kino International's DVD edition carries new intertitles Â© 2008 Kino International Corp. and a commissioned musical score; Flicker Alley's Blu-ray release adds its own protected creative elements. Both editions are protected works-within-works through at least 2103. Producers who want to use this film without a license should source from the Internet Archive transfer (archived May 2013, identifier THEEXTRAGIRL1923MabelNormandRalphGravesGeorgeNichols), which predates the commercial restorations and carries no restoration copyright notice, then supply an original or public-domain score. Any audio track pulled from a Kino or Flicker Alley copy must be licensed separately from the footage.
faq: Can I use the Kino DVD version of The Extra Girl in my documentary?

Not without a license for Kino's additions. The 1923 footage is public domain, but the Kino DVD includes new intertitles (Â© 2008 Kino International Corp.) and a commissioned musical score, both of which are protected independently of the film itself. Source your footage from the Internet Archive transfer instead and supply your own score or public-domain music.
Can I sell a VOD or physical release built around The Extra Girl?

Yes, using the underlying 1923 footage from a public-domain source such as the Internet Archive transfer. You cannot replicate the Kino or Flicker Alley editions because their intertitles, scores, and restoration creative choices are protected. Add your own title cards and score, and the print and story layers are clearâ€”though verify current right-of-publicity law in your target jurisdiction regarding Mabel Normand's likeness in commercial contexts.
